correctness.rationale: The falling-factorial series converges with all required derivatives and interpolates signed derangements. Its unit branch is an isometry onto \(1+3\mathbb Z_3\). The exact derivative congruences \(F\prime(1)\equiv9\pmod{27}\) and \(F\prime\prime(1)/2\equiv1\pmod3\) give a unique critical point \(c=1+9w\) and \(F(c)=81u\) with \(u\equiv2\pmod3\). A p-adic square-coordinate change gives the quadratic image, whose sign-pair overlap is exactly \(27\mathbb Z_3\). The square-count recurrence yields the formula for every positive exponent and Haar measure \(725/972\). A standalone verifier independently enumerated the recurrence through full periods for exponents one to eight and checked derivatives.

value.rationale: The exact residue-image cardinalities and p-adic Haar measure are natural arithmetic distribution invariants for a classical combinatorial number-theory sequence. The singular quadratic branch creates the nontrivial Haar measure \(725/972\) and necessitates a precise intersection of translated square images. The result gives a complete infinite prime-power classification, not a slight finite cutoff improvement.
